objective: Choose the S1 field-inversion regularization from prior theory rather than from convention, and report posterior uncertainty on the correction field instead of a point field, using the regularization provenance the weighted arm already wrote down as the design input
rationale: The S1 line closed end to end with both gates failing for measured reasons and with the successor arm filed, unrun, and its trigger routed explicitly to this design phase, so this item is not a new idea but the named unblock of an existing hold. The material it needs is already tabulated. The provenance table carries three runs with their objective weights and their penalty weights, the ground each was chosen on, and the achieved penalty share, and all three sit below the convention the reference method uses, which is the honest way of saying the choices were made by defensible habit rather than by theory. The Bayesian reading is already written into the same record: the penalty toward unity is a Gaussian prior on the correction field whose precision is set by the penalty weight and the noise scale, the bounds truncate that prior, and between 212 and 224 cells sit on the lower bound in every converged field, which is exactly the posterior mass a truncation hides and a point field cannot show. Better still, the record contains an observation a posterior treatment can be graded against rather than merely compared with: in the first run the optimisation plateaued where the penalty gradient and the objective gradient cancelled at a norm ratio near unity, with a root-mean-square near 0.0165, and the record names that as the calibration point a posterior treatment should reproduce. The failed gates give the design its shape too. The first gate missed at 0.05713 against a bar of 0.05320, a factor of 1.074, while still descending at roughly 0.004 per evaluation when the budget guard stopped it, so the loss was not converged and a posterior built at that point must say so. The second gate reports 42.7 percent inside the metric window against 79.7 percent inside the loss support, which is the loss-support versus metric-support question the held arm exists to answer and which a prior specification has to decide anyway. Axis A: reading-kind, priced from measured per-evaluation cost on this exact case. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0, and the in-sample position is stated below. DESIGN RULING ADDED 2026-08-11, pre-registration section 5, because this phase was named as the trigger for the held W1-only arm on the grounds that it must decide loss support anyway. It does: do not narrow the loss, replace the mask with a noise model. A hard 0/1 spatial mask is the assertion that sigma is infinite outside the box, i.e. that free-channel data carries no information about beta, and the measured evidence contradicts the strong form of that -- the equal-weight inversion moved the free-channel residual by -21.6 percent. What the data supports is the weaker quantitative statement that those observations are noisier because they are dominated by reference-interpolation error, which a heteroscedastic sigma(x) expresses directly and which DERIVES the down-weighting the weighted arm imposed by hand. Consequence for the docket: the W1-only arm's hard window mask is the sigma-to-infinity limit of this arm's noise model, so it is a special case of this arm rather than an independent experiment, and the recommendation is to CLOSE IT AS ABSORBED. That is a recommendation to the chief and not a decision taken here -- the arm was held by a chief ruling and only the chief closes it.

cost_basis: REPRICED 2026-08-11 from 150 against a capability limit found in the run directories, and the superseded basis is stated so the change is auditable. The filed basis read that the posterior analysis 'rides the arm's converged fields at no additional solver time'. Converged FIELDS are on disk; CURVATURE is not. Both drivers delete the per-evaluation gradient immediately after use (invert_lbfgsb.py line 97, os.remove(gpath), 'keep every 10th + eval001'), so 14 of 16 gradients were discarded in each run and the L-BFGS (s,y) pairs are not reconstructible: s_k is available from the eleven beta_accept_iter*.npy files, y_k = g_(k+1) - g_k is not. A posterior needs second-order information and the second-order information this family generated was not retained. New basis, all measured on this exact case: ~20 core-min per compute_totals at -primalTol 1e-8, --cpus=2 (the reinversion billed 320.13 for 16 evaluations = 20.0 each; the tightened tolerance is why the price rose from the corrupted run's 16.4). DAFoam exposes no second-order adjoint on this configuration -- the driver's only solver task is compute_totals -- so each Hessian-vector product is a one-sided finite difference of the gradient, one compute_totals, ~20 core-min. Laplace posterior at rank r=20 with oversampling p=4: base gradient re-anchor 20 + 24 HVPs at 20 = 480 + eigen-analysis, credible intervals and one field write-out ~15 = 515, plus 45 headroom (8.7 percent, sized on this family's own contention history -- the weighted arm's first two evaluations billed 27.1 and 26.5 against an 18.9 uncontended basis under A3 contention, a ~40 percent per-eval penalty that ate its eighth evaluation) = 560 hard cap. Tier 1 (the implied-prior audit, the theory derivation, the truncation accounting and the plateau-balance control) is ZERO core-min and is already executed in the pre-registration. At the previously filed 150 the affordable rank is r~5 on a 21,000-dimensional field, which is a token rather than a posterior, and a rank-5 credible interval reported as a credible interval is the kind of number this lab exists to not produce. The re-inversion under the theory prior (~230 core-min) is deliberately NOT folded in: it is a separate decision to be taken after the posterior exists, because the posterior is what says whether it is worth buying.
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes with different consequences, and the falsifiers are named in the pre-registration section 6 so the stage can fail. One: the posterior credible intervals straddle unity in a majority of separated-flow window cells, which would mean the measured 94.9 percent window error reduction is a fit the data does not constrain and the point field cannot be published as an identified correction. Two: the leading prior-preconditioned Hessian eigenvalues show no decay, which would mean the problem is not effectively low-dimensional, no affordable finite-rank posterior is defensible, and the obstruction is the parameterization rather than the objective or the prior, promoting the Dow-style nu_t-discrepancy alternative from named to indicated. Three: the derived prior collapses the window fix below 50 percent reduction, which would mean the correction was carried by an almost-flat prior doing load-bearing work nobody accounted for. The merely disappointing outcome, distinct from all three, is that the derived weight lands near the value in use, the pinning drops as predicted, and the gates land where they already are -- confirming the convention was defensible by luck, and giving this line its first derived prior. Either way the truncated prior mass gets a number: the weight in use corresponds to a Gaussian prior with standard deviation 0.676 on a positive multiplier, which places 6.96 percent of its mass on physically impossible negative production and 11.85 percent below the pre-registered lower bound. FALSIFIER, stated as distinct from a disappointing result: if the 95 percent posterior credible interval for beta includes 1 in 50 percent or more of the separated-flow window cells, the data does not identify a correction where the physics says the model error lives, every point field this family has produced is a regularization artifact in the window, and the -94.9 percent window error reduction is a statement about the flexibility of 21,000 free parameters rather than about closure physics. That ends the production-term line and it is read directly off gate (b)'s output. Three further falsifiers are pre-registered: the theory-prior posterior mean departing from the white-prior MAP by more than a posterior standard deviation in the window (the earlier fields were prior-determined); gate (c) failing (the machinery does not describe the optimization actually run); and the y>2 residual showing mesh-scale spatial correlation, which would mean the free-channel term is unmodelled structure rather than noise and this arm's heteroscedastic design is invalid as specified. Merely disappointing, and explicitly NOT falsifiers: the theory prior landing near the conventional 1e-5, a well-constrained posterior that still fails G2, or an inadequate rank-20 truncation.

gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Bayesian inverse problems: Stuart's acta numerica / Kaipio-Somersalo -> PROOF: S1's regularization chosen by theory (prior interpretation), posterior uncertainty on beta reported, not just a point field.' Operationalised into four pre-registered gates in S1_PRIORS_PREREGISTRATION.md section 4, all required. G-P1: the penalty weight is derived from a stated prior and a measured noise scale, reported against the three values already used and across the pre-registered noise band; a value chosen to match a previous run fails. Note the derivation is already executed and lands at 8.13e-06, which is 0.81x the 1e-05 in use, so the MAGNITUDE agreeing with convention is pre-declared and cannot later be presented as a derivation triumph -- the experiment is the prior's FORM. G-P2: the lognormal prior's restoring pull at the lower bound is 8.2x the Gaussian's, so the pre-stated prediction is that cells pinned at 0.2 fall from 223 to fewer than 60; PASS below 60, graded a wrong prediction at or above 223. G-P3: the reported product is per-cell credible intervals over all 21,000 cells plus the truncation mass plus the leading prior-preconditioned Hessian spectrum the intervals were built from; asserted error bars fail. G-P4: the posterior reproduces the corrupted run's plateau balance, re-based onto the exact analytic |g_penalty| = 4.785304e-04 computed from the archived beta field rather than onto the published ratio-and-cosine pair, which the pre-registration shows is not self-consistent (docket D8); recovery to 1 percent required or the posterior is reported as failing its own control. BARS FIXED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION (S1_WITH_PRIORS_PREREGISTRATION.md, sections 7 and 8), all committed before any solve. (a) is met in advance by construction and recorded as such so no later reader has to wonder whether it was fitted afterwards: the derivation yields lambda_L2 = 3.349e-05 at prior sd 0.35 in log space, band 1.64e-05 to 6.56e-05, against the 1e-4 and 1e-5 the family actually used. (b) carries a pre-registered failure label: if the 20th eigenvalue of the prior-preconditioned misfit Hessian has not fallen below 1, the posterior is reported RANK-LIMITED and its intervals labelled lower bounds on width. (c) bar is quantitative: |g_pen|/|g_QoI| and rms|beta-1| within 2 percent of 0.998441 and 0.016502, both measured from disk at zero compute in the pre-registration. G1 is deliberately NOT carried into this arm -- a MAP under a different prior is not comparable to the old one on a normalized-QoI bar, and reporting J_qoi against 0.70 here would inherit a number nobody re-derived for this prior. G2 IS carried unchanged at >50 percent, argued rather than assumed: it is the only bar in the family independent of both the loss and the prior, it survived the objective repair, and its two failures were each explained by a mechanism measured afterwards rather than by the bar being wrong.
